components: a central upright ending in a short angular tail
strokeOrder: start at the top left and draw the left upright straight down
without lifting, climb back up the upright and carry the top bar to the right
without lifting, return along the bar to the middle and draw the central upright down
without lifting, add the short angular tail down-left and hook its tip down-right — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: one stroke — the manual numbers four movements; native writers draw them without lifting, and this ductus follows them in order, climbing back up the left upright to start the top bar; cited to Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Frame 3, ர

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 3, ர (University of Texas at Austin), p. 191
strokeOrderSource.variation: Frame 3 identifies ர as the three-movement ஈ frame plus a slightly angular short fourth movement. Native writers draw the four movements as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows them in order without lifting: the first movement runs down the left upright, so the pen climbs back up it to begin the top bar and returns along the bar to the central upright. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 90% of the 189 stored prototypes of ர are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline.

notes: The light/flapped r, distinct from ற. The upright and cap come first; the pen then descends through the middle and stays on the paper through the small angular tail.
